ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the image is an ordinary clock face, with 12 marked at the top and 1 marked at the upper right. A dashed line represents a vertical line from the center of the clock face pointing toward the 12 o'clock direction. The longer minute hand is on the left side of the vertical line, close to the 11 o'clock direction; the shorter hour hand is on the right side of the vertical line, close to the 1 o'clock direction. Two identical angle markings in the image indicate that the angle between the minute hand and the vertical line is equal to the angle between the hour hand and the vertical line. Reasoning: The class starts at noon 12:00 and lasts 1 hour, so the observation time is between 12:00 and 1:00. Suppose the observation moment is t minutes after noon. The hour hand turns 0.5 degrees per minute, so the hour hand has turned clockwise by 0.5t degrees relative to the vertical 12 o'clock direction. The minute hand turns 6 degrees per minute; because in the image the minute hand is on the left side of the vertical line, close to the 11 o'clock direction, its smaller angle relative to the vertical line is 360 - 6t degrees. According to the equal-angle condition in the image: 360 - 6t = 0.5t. Solving gives 360 = 6.5t, so t = 360 / 6.5 = 720/13 minutes. The time remaining until the class ends is 60 - 720/13 = 60/13 minutes. Converted into seconds, this is (60/13) × 60 = 3600/13 ≈ 276.923 seconds. Therefore the remaining whole seconds, that is, complete seconds, is 276.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a normal clock face: the dashed vertical line is the 12 o’clock direction, the longer minute hand is to the left of vertical, and the shorter hour hand is to the right of vertical, with equal marked angles to the vertical. From the text, the lesson began at midday and lasts one hour, so the time is between 12:00 and 1:00. Let t be the number of minutes after midday. In this interval the hour hand is 0.5t degrees clockwise from vertical. Since the minute hand is on the left side near 11, its angle from vertical is 360 - 6t degrees. Use the image’s equal-angle condition: 360 - 6t = 0.5t. Solve for t, then subtract from 60 minutes and convert the remaining fractional minutes to seconds; take the number of whole seconds remaining.
